events.title: Israelites Settle Canaan
events.description: According to the Bible and archaeological evidence, Hebrew tribes began settling Canaan (modern Israel/Palestine) in the Late Bronze Age. These early Israelites formed tribal confederacy, gradually developed unique monotheistic faith worshiping Yahweh (YHWH). Canaanite city-states like Megiddo and Hazor declined during this period.

events.title: King David Unites Israel
events.description: King David unified the Israelite and Judah tribes, establishing a united kingdom with Jerusalem as capital. David conquered the Jebusite fortress, brought the Ark of the Covenant to Jerusalem, making it the religious and political center. David holds central position in Jewish tradition, seen as ancestor of the Messiah.

events.title: Solomon Builds the Temple
events.description: King Solomon built the First Temple in Jerusalem, becoming Judaism's holiest site. Solomon's reign was Israel's golden age, known for wisdom, wealth and trade with foreign nations. Solomon established relations with Egypt, Tyre and Sheba.

events.title: Kingdom Divides
events.description: After Solomon's death, kingdom split into northern Kingdom of Israel (capital Samaria) and southern Kingdom of Judah (capital Jerusalem). Two kingdoms often conflicted, faced threats from Assyria and later Babylon.

events.title: Assyria Destroys Kingdom of Israel
events.description: Assyrian Empire conquered northern Kingdom of Israel, destroyed Samaria. Ten tribes were exiled, becoming legendary 'Lost Ten Tribes.' Only southern Kingdom of Judah survived, preserving Jewish tradition.

events.title: Babylonian Captivity
events.description: Babylonian Nebuchadnezzar II conquered Judah, destroyed Jerusalem and the First Temple. Jewish elites were exiled to Babylon. This exile profoundly influenced Judaism, prompting compilation of the Torah and development of synagogue system.

events.title: Persia Allows Jewish Return
events.description: After conquering Babylon, Persian King Cyrus allowed Jews to return to Judah, rebuild the Temple. Second Temple completed in 516 BCE. Ezra and Nehemiah led religious and social reforms, strengthening Jewish identity.

events.title: Alexander's Conquest
events.description: Alexander the Great conquered Persian Empire, Judea entered Hellenistic period. Greek culture influenced Jewish society, triggering tensions between traditionalists and Hellenizers.

events.title: Maccabean Revolt
events.description: Seleucid King Antiochus IV attempted forced Hellenization and desecrated Temple, triggering revolt led by Maccabee family. Jews miraculously defeated Seleucid army, recaptured Jerusalem, rededicated Temple. This event commemorated by Hanukkah.

events.title: Hasmonean Dynasty
events.description: After Maccabean Revolt, Hasmonean family established independent Jewish kingdom, first Jewish sovereignty since First Temple destruction. Kingdom expanded territory but internal factional struggles weakened state.

events.title: Roman Conquest
events.description: Roman general Pompey conquered Judea, exploiting Hasmonean civil war. Judea became Roman client state, later province. Herod the Great ruled with Roman support, rebuilt and expanded Temple.

events.title: Crucifixion of Jesus
events.description: Jesus of Nazareth was crucified under Roman governor Pontius Pilate. Jesus's followers believed he resurrected, forming Christianity, new religion that eventually separated from Judaism, spreading throughout Roman Empire.

events.title: First Jewish-Roman War
events.description: Jews revolted against Roman rule. Romans brutally suppressed, in 70 CE Titus besieged Jerusalem, destroyed Second Temple. Only Western Wall (Wailing Wall) survived. Jewish defenders at Masada fortress committed mass suicide. Temple destruction marked fundamental transformation of Judaism.

events.title: Bar Kokhba Revolt
events.description: Jews launched second major revolt against Rome led by Simon bar Kokhba. Romans crushed revolt, Hadrian banned Jews from Jerusalem, renamed Judea to Syria Palaestina. This marked end of ancient Jewish national existence, beginning of diaspora era.

events.title: Compilation of Mishnah and Talmud
events.description: In Galilee and Babylon, rabbis compiled oral law into Mishnah and Talmud. These texts became foundation of Rabbinic Judaism, allowing Judaism to survive and thrive without Temple. This period saw Judaism transform from Temple-centered religion to text and learning-based tradition.

events.title: Muslim Conquest of Jerusalem
events.description: Arab Muslims conquered Jerusalem from Byzantines. Caliph Omar entered Jerusalem, guaranteed religious freedom for Jews and Christians. Muslims built Dome of the Rock on Temple Mount. Palestine became part of Islamic world for next 13 centuries.

events.title: Crusaders Capture Jerusalem
events.description: First Crusade captured Jerusalem, massacring Muslim and Jewish inhabitants. Crusaders established Latin Kingdom of Jerusalem. Jews were banned from city, scattered to other Middle Eastern regions.

events.title: Saladin Recaptures Jerusalem
events.description: Saladin defeated Crusaders at Hattin, recaptured Jerusalem. Unlike Crusaders, Saladin allowed Jews to return to city. Jerusalem became important Muslim pilgrimage site.

events.title: Ottoman Rule Begins
events.description: Ottoman Empire conquered Palestine from Mamluks. Ottoman rule lasted 400 years, bringing stability and allowing Jewish immigration. Suleiman the Magnificent rebuilt Jerusalem's walls. Jewish community in Safed flourished, becoming center of Kabbalah mysticism.

events.title: First Aliyah (Immigration Wave)
events.description: First major Jewish immigration wave from Eastern Europe, escaping pogroms. About 25,000-35,000 Jews immigrated, establishing agricultural settlements. This marked beginning of modern Zionist settlement in Palestine.

events.title: Herzl's 'The Jewish State'
events.description: Theodor Herzl published 'Der Judenstaat' (The Jewish State), proposing establishment of sovereign Jewish state as solution to anti-Semitism. This influential book laid ideological foundation for political Zionism. Herzl argued assimilation failed, Jews needed own homeland to escape persecution.

events.title: First Zionist Congress
events.description: Theodor Herzl convened First Zionist Congress in Basel, Switzerland. Congress established World Zionist Organization, declared goal to create 'publicly secured and legally assured home for Jewish people in Palestine.' Zionism transformed from scattered idea into organized political movement.

events.title: Second Aliyah
events.description: About 40,000 Jews immigrated, mainly from Russia after 1905 revolution failure. This wave brought socialist and Labor Zionist ideologies, founded kibbutzim. David Ben-Gurion and Yitzhak Ben-Zvi arrived during this period.

events.title: Founding of Tel Aviv
events.description: Jewish residents of Jaffa founded Tel Aviv, first modern Jewish city. Starting as garden suburb, Tel Aviv rapidly grew into economic and cultural center of Yishuv. It symbolized Zionist vision of creating new Hebrew society in ancient homeland.

events.title: Balfour Declaration
events.description: British Foreign Secretary Balfour declared Britain's support for 'establishment in Palestine of a national home for the Jewish people.' This gave Zionist movement international recognition. But declaration also promised not to prejudice Arab population rights, planting seeds of future conflict.

events.title: British Occupation of Palestine
events.description: British forces under General Allenby defeated Ottomans, occupied Palestine. Allenby's entry into Jerusalem ended 400 years of Ottoman rule. British control set stage for implementing Balfour Declaration and future conflicts between Jewish and Arab national aspirations.

events.title: British Mandate
events.description: League of Nations granted Britain mandate over Palestine. Britain permitted Jewish immigration but limited it under Arab pressure. This period saw Jewish-Arab tensions escalate, multiple riots and revolts. Jewish community (Yishuv) built self-governing institutions, defense forces (Haganah).

events.title: Third Aliyah
events.description: About 35,000 Jews immigrated after World War I and Russian Revolution. Many were young Zionist pioneers (halutzim) fleeing pogroms and Soviet anti-religious policies. They established more kibbutzim and developed Hebrew culture, but faced economic hardship.

events.title: Hebron Massacre
events.description: Arab riots erupted over Western Wall dispute, killing 67 Jews in Hebron. This ended centuries-old Jewish community there. Violence spread to other cities, deepening Jewish-Arab rift.

events.title: Fifth Aliyah and Nazi Persecution
events.description: Over 250,000 Jews fled to Palestine escaping Nazi persecution in Germany and Eastern Europe. This wave included many professionals, intellectuals and middle-class families. They brought capital, skills and culture, transforming Palestine's economy and urban development. But mounting Arab opposition led Britain to restrict immigration.

events.title: Arab Revolt
events.description: Palestinian Arabs revolted against British rule and Jewish immigration. Britain brutally suppressed revolt, Arab leadership was decimated. To appease Arabs, Britain issued 1939 White Paper severely limiting Jewish immigration, angering Zionists when Holocaust began.

events.title: White Paper Restricts Immigration
events.description: Britain issued 1939 White Paper severely restricting Jewish immigration to Palestine to 75,000 over five years, then requiring Arab consent. This betrayed Balfour Declaration and blocked Jewish refuge just as Holocaust began. Zionists condemned it as moral betrayal during Jews' darkest hour.

events.title: Holocaust
events.description: Nazi Germany systematically murdered 6 million Jews, two-thirds of European Jewry. Holocaust gave moral urgency to Zionist cause. Survivors desperately sought refuge in Palestine, but British continued blocking immigration.

events.title: Jewish Armed Struggle
events.description: Jewish underground organizations (Irgun, Lehi) launched armed campaign against British rule, bombing King David Hotel and other targets. Haganah organized illegal immigration (Aliyah Bet) smuggling Holocaust survivors. British responded with repression but ultimately decided to withdraw, referring issue to UN.

events.title: UN Partition Plan
events.description: UN proposed dividing Palestine into Jewish and Arab states, with Jerusalem internationalized. Jews accepted, Arabs rejected. Plan allocated 56% territory to Jewish state (with 33% population). Intercommunal violence erupted immediately.

events.title: Declaration of State of Israel
events.description: Before British Mandate ended, Ben-Gurion declared establishment of State of Israel in Tel Aviv. Israel became the first Jewish sovereign state in nearly 2000 years. US and USSR quickly recognized it. But Arab states invaded the next day, War of Independence erupted.

events.title: War of Independence (First Arab-Israeli War)
events.description: Israel fought against Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Iraq and Lebanon coalition. War occurred in several phases, Israel ultimately won, expanding territory beyond partition plan. About 700,000 Palestinian Arabs fled or were expelled, becoming refugees (Palestinians call it 'Nakba' - catastrophe).

events.title: Armistice Agreements and Law of Return
events.description: Israel signed armistice agreements with neighbors, establishing ceasefire lines (Green Line). Israel passed Law of Return, granting all Jews right to immigrate to Israel. Hundreds of thousands of Jewish refugees and Holocaust survivors flooded in from Europe, Middle East and North Africa.

events.title: Operation Magic Carpet and Middle East Jewish Immigration
events.description: Israel organized massive airlifts, bringing Yemeni Jews (Operation Magic Carpet) and Iraqi Jews (Operations Ezra and Nehemiah) to Israel. Jews from Arab countries immigrated en masse amid hostility and persecution, transforming Israel's demographic composition.

events.title: Suez Crisis (Sinai Campaign)
events.description: After Nasser nationalized Suez Canal, Israel joined UK and France in invading Egypt. Israel quickly captured Sinai Peninsula but US-Soviet pressure forced withdrawal. Though brief, war demonstrated Israel's military capabilities.

events.title: Capture and Trial of Eichmann
events.description: Israeli Mossad kidnapped Nazi war criminal Eichmann in Argentina, brought him to Israel for trial. 1961 trial drew global attention, exposed Holocaust horrors. Eichmann was sentenced to death and executed, Israel's only ever execution.

events.title: Six-Day War
events.description: After escalating tensions, Israel launched preemptive strikes against Egypt, Syria and Jordan. In just 6 days, Israel destroyed Arab air forces, captured Sinai, Golan Heights, West Bank and East Jerusalem. This lightning victory completely changed Middle East landscape, but also began moral and security dilemmas of occupation.

events.title: Unification of Jerusalem
events.description: Israeli paratroopers captured East Jerusalem and Temple Mount, unifying city. For first time in nearly 2000 years Jews controlled Western Wall and Temple Mount. But Israel's annexation of East Jerusalem not internationally recognized, Jerusalem's status became core peace process dispute.

events.title: Yom Kippur War
events.description: Egypt and Syria launched surprise attack on Yom Kippur (holiest Jewish holiday). Israel initially caught off guard but eventually counterattacked and repelled invasion. War shattered Israel's invincibility myth, caused heavy casualties, triggered political upheaval.

events.title: Entebbe Raid
events.description: Palestinian and German terrorists hijacked Air France flight, landing it in Entebbe, Uganda. Israeli commandos executed bold long-distance rescue operation, freeing over 100 hostages. Operation became symbol of Israel's counterterrorism capabilities.

events.title: Likud Comes to Power
events.description: Menachem Begin's right-wing Likud won election for first time, ending Labor's nearly 30-year rule. This marked major shift in Israeli politics toward more hardline nationalism and settlement expansion policies.

events.title: Sadat Visits Jerusalem
events.description: Egyptian President Sadat suddenly visited Jerusalem, addressed Israeli Knesset. This historic visit broke psychological barriers, paved way for Egypt-Israel peace, shocked Arab world.

events.title: Camp David Accords and Egypt-Israel Peace Treaty
events.description: Mediated by President Carter, Sadat and Begin reached peace framework at Camp David. In 1979 two countries signed peace treaty, Israel returned Sinai, Egypt recognized Israel. This was first Arab-Israeli peace treaty, but Sadat was assassinated for it.

events.title: Bombing Iraq's Nuclear Reactor
events.description: Israeli Air Force bombed Iraq's Osirak nuclear reactor, destroying Saddam's nuclear program. This preemptive strike was internationally condemned but later seen as preventing nuclear proliferation in Middle East.

events.title: Lebanon Invasion
events.description: Israel invaded Lebanon aiming to eliminate PLO. Israel besieged Beirut, forced PLO evacuation. But war became quagmire, Sabra and Shatila massacre (by Lebanese Christian militias, Israel accused of failing to prevent) drew international condemnation and domestic protests.

events.title: First Intifada
events.description: Palestinians launched mass uprising in occupied territories, using stones, strikes and civil disobedience. Israeli military violently suppressed, drawing international criticism. Intifada changed Israeli-Palestinian conflict, drew international attention to Palestinian plight, prompted peace process.

events.title: Gulf War and Scud Missiles
events.description: During Gulf War, Iraq fired Scud missiles at Israel, trying to drag Israel into war and break Arab coalition. Under US pressure, Israel showed restraint and didn't retaliate. After war, US pushed for Middle East peace conference.

events.title: Mass Immigration of Soviet Jews
events.description: After Soviet collapse, about 1 million Soviet Jews immigrated to Israel. This massive immigration significantly increased Israel's population, brought technological and cultural capital, but also intensified settlement expansion and tensions with Palestinians.

events.title: Oslo Accords
events.description: PM Rabin and Chairman Arafat shook hands on White House lawn, signing Oslo Accords. Israel recognized PLO, PLO recognized Israel, agreed to gradually establish Palestinian self-government. This brought hope for peace, but implementation was fraught with difficulties.

events.title: Peace Treaty with Jordan
events.description: Israel signed peace treaty with Jordan, second Arab-Israeli peace treaty. King Hussein and Rabin established close relationship. Treaty resolved border and water issues, opened economic cooperation.

events.title: Rabin Assassinated
events.description: PM Rabin was assassinated by far-right Jewish extremist Yigal Amir after Tel Aviv peace rally. Rabin's death shocked Israel, peace process lost key driver. Many believe this marked the end of Oslo peace process.

events.title: Camp David Summit Fails
events.description: Clinton convened Barak and Arafat at Camp David for final status negotiations. Though close to agreement, failed to reach consensus on key issues like Jerusalem's status. After summit failure, Second Intifada erupted.

events.title: Second Intifada (Al-Aqsa Intifada)
events.description: Sharon's visit to Temple Mount triggered Palestinian uprising, more violent than the first. Palestinian suicide bombings killed hundreds of Israeli civilians. Israeli military operations and targeted killings killed thousands of Palestinians. Violence cycle destroyed peace hopes.

events.title: Begin Building Separation Barrier
events.description: Israel began building separation barrier in West Bank (Israel calls security fence, Palestinians call apartheid wall). Israel said it prevented terror attacks, suicide bombings indeed decreased dramatically. But barrier penetrates deep into West Bank, divides Palestinian communities, International Court of Justice ruled it illegal.

events.title: Disengagement from Gaza
events.description: PM Sharon unilaterally withdrew from Gaza Strip, evacuating all settlements and troops. This controversial decision divided Israeli society. Disengagement didn't bring peace, instead led to Hamas takeover and subsequent blockade.

events.title: Second Lebanon War
events.description: Hezbollah cross-border raid and kidnapping of Israeli soldiers triggered 34-day war. Israel bombed Lebanese infrastructure, ground invasion of south. War caused major destruction but no clear victory, Israel criticized for poor preparation, Hezbollah claimed resistance victory.

events.title: Hamas Takes Control of Gaza
events.description: Hamas defeated Fatah in Gaza, controlling Gaza Strip. Israel imposed tight blockade on Gaza, controlling borders, airspace and waters. Palestinians split between West Bank (Fatah controlled) and Gaza (Hamas controlled), peace process paralyzed.

events.title: Gaza War (Operation Cast Lead)
events.description: Israel launched massive military operation against Gaza, responding to Hamas rocket attacks. Three-week operation killed over 1,400 Palestinians. UN report accused both sides of war crimes. This began series of conflicts between Israel and Hamas.

events.title: Netanyahu Returns as PM
events.description: Benjamin Netanyahu led Likud back to power, becoming Israel's longest-serving PM (until 2021, then again from 2022). Netanyahu took hardline positions, expanded settlements, opposed Palestinian statehood, but normalized relations with Arab states.

events.title: Mavi Marmara Incident
events.description: Israeli commandos intercepted Turkish flotilla trying to break Gaza blockade, killing 10 Turkish activists on Mavi Marmara. Incident severely damaged Israeli-Turkish relations (only restored in 2016), drew international criticism of Gaza blockade.

events.title: Repeated Conflicts with Hamas
events.description: Israel fought multiple military conflicts with Hamas in Gaza. 2014 'Operation Protective Edge' lasted 50 days, killing over 2,200 Palestinians and 70+ Israelis. Each conflict was cycle of rockets and airstrikes, causing civilian casualties but failing to resolve fundamental issues.

events.title: US Moves Embassy to Jerusalem
events.description: President Trump moved US Embassy from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem, recognizing Jerusalem as Israel's capital. Decision welcomed by Israel but angered Palestinians and Arab world, seen as biased toward Israel.

events.title: Abraham Accords
events.description: Under Trump administration's push, Israel normalized relations with UAE, Bahrain, Morocco and Sudan. These Abraham Accords broke traditional Arab stance (solve Palestinian issue first before establishing ties with Israel), reshaping Middle East relations.

events.title: Political Crisis and Bennett Government
events.description: After four inconclusive elections and political deadlock, Netanyahu was ousted. Naftali Bennett led diverse coalition government, including for first time an Arab party. But coalition fragile, dissolved in 2022, Netanyahu returned.

events.title: Judicial Reform Controversy
events.description: Netanyahu government pushed controversial judicial reforms attempting to weaken Supreme Court powers. This triggered largest protests in Israeli history, hundreds of thousands took to streets. Reform criticized as undermining democracy, society deeply divided.

events.title: Hamas Attack and Israel-Hamas War
events.description: Hamas launched massive raid from Gaza, killing about 1200 Israelis, kidnapping about 250 hostages. This was the worst terrorist attack in Israeli history. Israel launched massive military operation in Gaza, vowing to destroy Hamas. War caused tens of thousands of Palestinian deaths in Gaza, massive destruction and humanitarian disaster.

events.title: Ongoing War and Regional Tensions
events.description: Israel-Hamas war continues, Gaza suffers devastating blow. Israel simultaneously conflicts with Lebanon's Hezbollah, Yemen's Houthis and Iran-backed militias. Regional tensions reach highest point in decades. War triggers international criticism of Israel, but also gains Western support. Hostage issue and Gaza reconstruction prospects unclear.
